claim: Peptidoglycan is an essential component of the bacterial cell envelope that surrounds the cytoplasmic membrane to protect the cell from osmotic lysis.
source: Peptidoglycan is an essential component of the bacterial cell envelope that surrounds the cytoplasmic membrane to protect the cell from osmotic lysis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about peptidoglycan function in bacteria.

claim: Important antibiotics such as β-lactams and glycopeptides target peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
source: Important antibiotics such as β-lactams and glycopeptides target peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about antibiotic mechanisms of action.

claim: Class A penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) are bifunctional membrane-bound peptidoglycan synthases that polymerize glycan chains and connect adjacent stem peptides by transpeptidation.
source: Class A penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) are bifunctional membrane-bound peptidoglycan synthases that polymerize glycan chains and connect adjacent stem peptides by transpeptidation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about class A PBP function.

claim: A novel Förster resonance energy transfer-based assay was developed to follow in real time both reactions of class A PBPs reconstituted in liposomes or supported lipid bilayers.
source: Here, we developed a novel Förster resonance energy transfer-based assay to follow in real time both reactions of class A PBPs reconstituted in liposomes or supported lipid bilayers
evidence: This is the main methodological contribution of the manuscript, supported by the experimental data presented throughout.

claim: The FRET assay was applied with PBP1B homologues from Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii in the presence or absence of their cognate lipoprotein activator.

claim: Peptidoglycan is composed of glycan strands of alternating N-actetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) and N-acetylmuramic acid (MurNAc) residues interconnected by short peptides.
source: It is composed of glycan strands of alternating N-actetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) and N-acetylmuramic acid (MurNAc) residues interconnected by short peptides.
evidence: This is established knowledge about peptidoglycan structure.

claim: PG forms a continuous, mesh-like layer around the cell membrane to protect the cell from bursting due to the turgor and maintain cell shape.
source: PG forms a continuous, mesh-like layer around the cell membrane to protect the cell from bursting due to the turgor and maintain cell shape (Vollmer et al., 2008).

source: First, most assays are end-point assays that rely on discrete sampling and therefore do not provide real-time information about the enzymatic reaction.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing methods.

claim: Some PG synthesis assays involve measuring the consumption of lipid II or analysing the reaction products by SDS-PAGE or HPLC after digestion with a muramidase.
source: Second, some assays involve measuring the consumption of lipid II or analysing the reaction products by SDS-PAGE (Egan et al., 2015; Barrett et al., 2007; Qiao et al., 2014; Sjodt et al., 2018) or high-pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) after digestion with a muramidase (Bertsche et al., 2005; Born et al., 2006).

claim: Laborious techniques for analyzing PG synthesis make assays incompatible with high-throughput screening and hinder the determination of kinetic parameters.
source: These laborious techniques make assays incompatible with high-throughput screening and hinder the determination of kinetic parameters.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of existing methods.

source: A simple, real-time assay with dansyl-labelled lipid II substrate overcomes these problems but is limited to assay GTase reactions (Schwartz et al., 2001; Offant et al., 2010; Egan et al., 2015).

claim: A real-time TPase assay uses non-natural mimics of TPase substrates such as the rotor-fluorogenic 470 D-lysine probe Rf470DL, which increases its fluorescence emission upon incorporation into PG.

claim: Both detergents and DMSO have been shown to affect the activity and interactions of E. coli PBP1B.

claim: A freely diffusing, detergent-solubilized membrane enzyme has a very different environment compared to the situation in the cell membrane where it contacts phospholipids and is confined in two dimensions.

claim: PBP1BEc can utilize fluorescently labelled lipid II to polymerize long glycan chains only when unlabelled lipid II is also present in the reaction.
source: PBP1BEc can utilize fluorescently labelled lipid II to polymerize long glycan chains only when unlabelled lipid II is also present in the reaction (Van't Veer et al., 2016).

claim: Both Atto550 and Atto647n probes were incorporated into the produced PG or glycan chains by PBP1BEc as indicated by SDS-PAGE analysis.
source: Both probes were incorporated into the produced PG or glycan chains as indicated by SDS-PAGE analysis (Figure 1B, I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: After the reaction of PBP1BEc with fluorescently labeled lipid II, fluorescence spectra showed a reduced donor emission intensity and an increased emission of the acceptor fluorophore, indicative of FRET between the two fluorophores.
source: After the reaction, fluorescence spectra taken at the excitation wavelength of the donor fluorophore (Atto550, λabs=552 nm) showed a reduced donor emission intensity (λfl=580 nm) and an increased emission of the acceptor fluorophore (Atto647n, λfl=665 nm) (Figure 1C, I) indicative of FRET between the two fluorophores.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: FRET efficiency for PBP1BEc reactions with fluorescently labeled lipid II was 29 ± 6%.

claim: Ampicillin blocked the formation of crosslinked PG by PBP1BEc and reduced the FRET efficiency to one third.

claim: Moenomycin completely abolished the incorporation of fluorescent lipid II by PBP1BEc and the associated FRET signal.

claim: Incorporation of the labelled probes into PG by PBP1BEc results in fluorescence energy transfer that depends on the GTase and TPase activity, with the latter being the major contributor.

claim: Moenomycin resulted in no FRET in samples containing detergent-solubilized PBP1BEc.

claim: Ampicillin generally reduced the final fluorescence ratio level by approximately threefold in reactions with detergent-solubilized PBP1BEc.

claim: The GTase reaction began after a lag phase, consistent with previously published data.
source: The GTase reaction began after a lag phase, consistent with previously published data (Schwartz et al., 2002; Egan et al., 2014)

claim: Slopes with LpoB were approximately ten- or twentyfold higher than without the activator, in the absence or presence of ampicillin, respectively.

claim: Inter-chain FRET is a major contributor to the final FRET signal.
